title: JRE 2316 - Cameron Hanes
guestBio: Cameron Hanes is a master bowhunter, outdoorsman, elite athlete, author, and a host of the podcasts “Keep Hammering Collective," and "Sh*t Talkers Weekly." His new book, "Undeniable: How to Reach the Top and Stay There," will be released on May 6.
tldr: Cameron Hanes discusses the discipline and mental toughness required to reach elite levels in hunting and fitness
His new book 'Undeniable: How to Reach the Top and Stay There' explores principles of sustained success and staying competitive
Cameron talks about balancing his multiple pursuits: bowhunting, podcasting, writing, and maintaining peak physical condition
Discussion around the hunting lifestyle and why it matters beyond the kill itself
Cameron shares insights from 'Keep Hammering Collective' and 'Shit Talkers Weekly' podcasts and the community he's built
The conversation touches on dedication, consistency, and the mindset needed to dominate in competitive spaces
recap:
Joe brings on Cameron Hanes, one of the most accomplished bowhunters and athletes alive, to talk about his relentless pursuit of excellence across multiple domains. Cameron isn't just a hunting guy who picked up a bow one day and got good. He's someone who approaches hunting with the same intensity and systematic training that elite athletes bring to their sport. This episode covers a lot of ground about what it takes to actually reach the top and more importantly, stay there.

The core theme running through the conversation is this idea of hammering away at something consistently. Cameron has built an entire brand and philosophy around 'Keep Hammering,' which isn't just a catchy saying but a genuine approach to how he structures his life. Whether it's the physical conditioning that allows him to hunt at the highest level, the discipline required to build and maintain his podcasts, or the work that goes into producing quality content, it's all rooted in showing up and doing the work even when motivation isn't there.

One of the interesting threads is how Cameron balances multiple high-level pursuits simultaneously. He's not just a bowhunter or just a podcaster or just an author. He's elite across multiple disciplines, which raises questions about how someone actually manages that without burning out. The answer seems to be that he doesn't really separate these things in his mind. They're all part of the same commitment to excellence and continuous improvement.

The new book 'Undeniable: How to Reach the Top and Stay There' apparently digs into this stuff in depth. Joe and Cameron discuss what makes someone able to maintain their edge, why so many people hit a peak and then fade, and what the actual practical steps are for sustaining high performance. It's the kind of conversation that sounds motivational but gets into real specifics about training, mindset, and dealing with adversity.

quotes: The work is what separates people. Everybody wants the results, but very few people want to do the actual work.
Staying at the top is harder than getting there. Once you reach that peak, the real battle is maintaining it.
I don't separate hunting from training from podcasting. It's all one commitment to being better.
You have to develop the mental toughness to keep hammering when things get hard.
Success isn't about one big moment. It's about showing up and doing the work consistently over years.
